questions.topic: Emergency safety incident storage without consent
questions.question: When the safety filter triggers (911/ER emergency), we store a de-identified truncated chat history and IP lock record in MongoDB without explicit user consent. Is this covered under HIPAA emergency exception? Do we need a disclosure notice?
questions.current_behavior: System stores de-identified incident record (IP, trigger message truncated to 500 chars, chat history truncated to 300 chars per message) in dev_Safety.emergency_incidents. No consent asked.
questions.risk: Medium - currently operating under assumption that HIPAA emergency exception applies

questions.topic: De-identification adequacy for HIPAA Safe Harbor
questions.question: Is our LLM-based deIdentify() function (Claude Haiku) sufficient to meet HIPAA Safe Harbor requirements? The function removes names, geographic identifiers, dates, phone, email, SSN, etc. but relies on LLM judgment rather than rule-based scrubbing.
questions.current_behavior: deIdentify() sends chat history to Claude Haiku with HIPAA Safe Harbor instructions. LLM returns scrubbed content. No validation that all 18 Safe Harbor identifiers are actually removed.
questions.risk: High - LLM may miss identifiers, no automated verification

questions.question: When a user consents to verbatim storage, the consent exchange is stored as part of chat_history. Is this sufficient as evidence of consent, or do we need a separate signed consent record?
questions.current_behavior: Consent question and user answer stored inline in chat_history array. No separate consent record or timestamp.
questions.risk: Medium - may not meet evidentiary standard for consent
